body:
> **The rule set below supersedes the Updated notes and the original policy wherever they differ.** IDs (G1, R3, C2, ...) are stable so rules can be adjusted individually.

## Rule set (sharpened 2026-11-04; operator-approved)

Sharpened by one Codex review round (gpt-6-astra, medium, relay `relay-system/2026-11-04/rules-sharpening-qa.md`; nine findings, all accepted) and approved by the operator together with retiring X5. Operator decisions keep their meaning; only wording, scope and interaction changed. **op** = operator decision; **agreed** = agreed between sessions.

### G: Governance (issues, docs, ledger)
- **G1 (op)** GitHub issue state is the only authority for "done". A doc's folder and its ledger section are views of it.
- **G2 (op)** Readers resolve a `GH-<n>-` doc by repository-qualified issue identity (`gh_issue`, else the filename prefix; `source` disambiguates a foreign repo). Stored paths are caches. Decided policy; today's path-based readers do not comply until #1340 Task 10.
- **G3 (op)** One idempotent sweep reads CLOSED issue state in `1-INBOX` and `2-WORKING`: `COMPLETED` -> `3-COMPLETED`, `NOT_PLANNED` -> `4-MISC`, OPEN or unknown stay (unknown is reported). It repoints only existing rows and never closes an issue. Until it lands (Task 9), the per-merge mover and drift reporter remain, gaps explicit.
- **G4 (op)** At merge, the orchestrator may close an issue only with (a) a recorded independent review assertion that the lane covers the whole issue, or (b) a non-empty Acceptance checklist with every item checked, and P5 where it applies. Otherwise leave it open with one "delivered, left open because ..." comment. A mention is never authority; write `Refs #N` and "leaves #N open", never a negated close keyword.
- **G5 (op)** Appeal stays neutral 50 unless the operator supplies a value.
- **G6 (op)** A PRS row and its stored rating are created when work starts, not at filing; until then the rating proposal lives in the issue body. Decided policy awaiting the cutover (see C2).
- **G6a (op)** The 69 existing "Queue / parked intake" rows stay as proposals; no migration; revisit about a month after the cutover. This exception does not grow.
- **G6b (op)** Selection means committing an issue to an actual execution batch or marathon, not ranking or shortlisting. At that point create its row on the primary, or reuse its existing proposal row and rating, before dispatch.

### R: Run rules
- **R1 (op)** During a run, repair routine, reversible implementation defects without asking when the repair restores already-agreed behaviour within the authorized scope. R2/W1 bound the attempts; R3/W2 exclude boundary changes.
- **R2 (op)** At most three diagnosis / targeted-repair / verification rounds per unresolved blocker, counted across sessions and wakes in existing run records. At exhaustion, file or update the issue, keep the milestone visibly blocked, and continue only independent eligible work.
- **R3 (op)** Ask the operator before: force push; deleting unlanded work; history rewrite; changing or bypassing what a check accepts; changing containment, sandbox, authentication or credential boundaries; ledger schema; merge policy; design or architecture; spending or access beyond existing authorization. Routine use of an already-authorized tool or account is not a boundary change.
- **R4 (op)** A run with agent repairs is reported as agent-assisted, never as unattended qualification.
- **R5 (op)** Before proposing a milestone, three lines: capability vs observed baseline; critical-path blocker it removes; evidence, budget and escalation. No separate document per milestone.
- **R6 (op, batch 1 only)** Merge batch PRs automatically once required checks and independent review pass. Merge permission does not authorize closing issues (G4/P5) and does not carry over to batch 2 without a new decision.
- **R7 (op, via this approval)** Run batch items one at a time; land prerequisite PRs through the normal review and merge rules first; before each item, refresh the disposable execution clone from `origin/development` only after preserving and reconciling any unique state in it. Ledger writes and checkpoints stay on the primary (C3). Do not overlap full-suite gates on one host. This allows no destructive reset, no merging of unrelated PRs, and no ban on intended parallel marathon lanes.

### P: Plan and ownership
- **P1 (agreed)** This session delivers #1340 Tasks 1-12 and evaluates closing #1333, #1340 and #1329 under G4/P5. Ownership is not advance closure approval.
- **P2 (agreed)** Order: Task 1 -> Task 10 -> Task 9 -> one cutover PR (Tasks 2, 3, 4, 6 + Task 11 rating contract, Task 5 as the #1298 rollout instruction) -> Task 7 -> Task 8 -> Task 12 -> #1332 item 2 -> #1298 batch 2.
- **P3 (agreed)** The cutover lands as one PR.
- **P4 (agreed)** Task 13 moves to its own dated issue.
- **P5 (agreed)** Close #1340, then #1333, only after reviewed evidence shows Tasks 1-12 merged, each with PR, merge SHA and a manual check under `TESTS-RESULTS/` with provenance. Close #1329 only after every batch-protocol idea is marked adopted or declined in #1298's batch 2 report. A partial task PR never closes these.
- **P6 (agreed)** Batch 2 waits for the cutover.
- **P7 (op)** The earlier request to register the 209 no-row issues is superseded by Task 5: prepare issue text, capture doc, contract and an issue-body rating proposal, without creating rows for intake, through the cutover-compatible intake path. C2 is not permission to bulk-register meanwhile.

### X: Specific items
- **X1 (op)** #670 deferred. **X2 (op, done)** #670 severity 60 -> 20.
- **X3 (op)** #1295 stays deferred; its fix is due **before** the first dispatch of a plan or launch packet generated by `factory-primitive` (the trigger as recorded on #1295, 2026-10-31).
- **X4 (op)** #1332 item 2 after the cutover.
- **X5 retired (op)** The 2026-10-31 restriction on long Mac Studio runs. Basis: admission measured (6/298) and landing proven (batch 1, 5 of 6). Retirement does not waive other run gates.

### Interim rules until the code catches up
- **C1** Until Task 7 lands, write a closing keyword only when G4 (and P5 where it applies) is met; otherwise `Refs #N`, "leaves #N open" and one reason comment. R6 governs merging, independently of closing.
- **C2** Today's intake tools and coverage checks still write and require rows at filing, so G6 waits for the cutover. Until a compatible intake path exists, do not run row-writing intake (`hq park --create` / `--gh-issue`, `/file-xyz-bug`, `express`) for new unstarted work. File the GitHub issue with its rating proposal in the body, and leave the capture doc and row to pickup. Do not relabel new rows as G6a proposals and do not weaken coverage.
- **C3** At committed selection, write or reuse rows on the primary and checkpoint them before dispatch, so the clean execution clone starts from that baseline; lanes never write the ledger. After landing, reconcile and checkpoint on the primary.
- **W1** R2's blocker rounds and each tool's own launch/round caps are separate budgets; stop when the next action would exceed either (Marathon's two lane fires are not two R2 rounds). Never bypass exhaustion with `--force`, raised caps, erased counters or new identities without operator approval, and never reset an R2 count because a tool reset its own.
- **W2** A runtime repair may restore a check's implementation to its agreed acceptance contract; changing that contract in either direction needs R3 approval.

---

## Updated notes (2026-11-04)

Review by the orchestrating session (Opus 5.5), applied while the six-issue landing batch from #1298 was running. The policy below stands; these notes adjust how it applies.

1. **Name one current objective.** Two are in play: the six-issue landing batch through the real Jog/Marathon loop (#1298, running since 2026-11-04 00:36Z) and the 24-hour unattended service qualification named below. The gates only work against one. **Current objective: finish the landing batch; the 24-hour qualification is the next agreed objective after it.** Until the operator says otherwise, the batch is the objective the gates are checked against.
2. **Label agent-assisted runs.** Under this policy's own definition, a run in which the orchestrator repairs on the fly is **agent-assisted**, not unattended. The #1298 batch is agent-assisted; its numbers are reported as such and are not cited as unattended qualification.
3. **Jog contradicts rule 4.** Rule 4 says to move to independent eligible work after stopping a blocker. Jog stops the whole queue on one failed task (observed 2026-11-04: #670's builder hang stopped all five items behind it). Until Jog has a continue-on-independent-failure mode, the orchestrator restarts the queue for the independent items and retries the blocked one at the end, recording the switch. A Jog change is a repair candidate if it recurs.
4. **This rounds rule replaces earlier limits.** The per-blocker rule here (a counted round = diagnosis, targeted repair, verification; at most three; no reset across sessions; then file an issue) supersedes the "3 adapt commits per item, 10 per batch, ~50 lines" limits set on 2026-11-03 in #1298. The one-way-door list there (force push, deleting unlanded work, history rewrite, weakening a check or `--no-verify`, containment/sandbox/auth/credentials, ledger schema, merge policy, design choices) stays as the escalation boundary; repairs are still captured as `adapt(GH-n): <symptom>` commits in the run PR.
5. **Keep the gates small.** The three gates are a three-line check at the top of a milestone proposal, not a new document per milestone. If applying them needs its own artifact, it has become the ceremony it was meant to stop.

6. **Lessons from the first batch (#1298, 5 of 6 landed, 2026-11-04).** No longer needed: repointing the ledger on a lane branch. Since #1339, a doc Jog promotes on an execution branch passes roadmap coverage as it is, and a lane-branch repoint breaks `jog resume` / `jog land`, so do not repeat it. Still apply: merge open PRs first and checkpoint the primary after (a checkpoint push conflicts every open PR's ledger); reset the execution clone's `development` to origin before each item (Jog commits onto it); run items one at a time; avoid two full-suite gates on one host at once.

## Background

The outer-loop effort needs to prove an inner-loop-agnostic service that wakes on schedule, maintains an honest heartbeat, evaluates state, executes one of four allowlisted custom scripts, writes to a predetermined location, and produces telemetry and observable receipts. The intended qualification milestone is a 24-hour unattended run before connecting XYZ Forge.

The operator reports that collaboration with Sonnet 5.5 repeatedly stopped on small issues and proposed small experiments that did not substantially advance that goal. The operator has switched to Opus 5.5 and authorized fixing system problems on the fly. This is context for the operating policy, not a general model-quality assessment.

The missing agreement is how to distinguish meaningful progress from activity, while giving the collaborator enough authority to finish work without repeatedly handing routine blockers back to the operator.

Related:
- [#1175: Hosted factory control plane over Jog](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1175)
- [#1188: Factory liveness and foreman dead-man's switch](https://github.com/HiQS-Labs/XYZ-forge/issues/1188)

## Goal

Require proposed milestones to deliver meaningful, verified progress toward the current agreed operational objective. Give the collaborator ownership of implementation and routine repairs, while preserving operator control over consequential changes and the integrity of acceptance evidence.

**Governing instruction:** Advance to the next observable capability. Fix routine blockers along the way rather than turning each blocker into a new experiment.

Apply these gates to all outer-loop milestones, not every troubleshooting action. A necessary small fix inherits the milestone's justification; it does not require a separate proposal or approval when it remains within authorized scope.

## Three qualifying gates

| Gate | Qualifying question | Passing answer |
|---|---|---|
| Outcome | What meaningful capability will work when this is finished that does not work now? | State the observed baseline and intended result: currently X; after this milestone Y; evidence Z. A document, configuration change, or component test alone is insufficient unless it resolves an explicit blocker to that result. |
| Critical path | Which current bottleneck to the agreed operational objective does this remove? | Work enables the objective, prevents an unsafe run, or makes the results trustworthy. Defer unrelated cleanup, extra adapters, dashboards, and speculative architecture. |
| Ownership and evidence | Can the collaborator carry this through implementation, bounded routine repairs, and verification without handing small problems back to the operator? | A bounded milestone with objective acceptance evidence, authority to fix reversible problems, a maximum of three repair rounds per unresolved blocker, and explicit stopping and escalation conditions. |

All three gates must pass before proposing a milestone. Name the current objective and observed baseline explicitly. The initial objective is the 24-hour unattended qualification run; after it, apply the rubric to the next explicitly agreed operational objective.

## Examples

- **Weak next step:** “Try a five-minute experiment to see whether scheduling works.” This demonstrates a fragment, not an operational capability.
- **Strong milestone:** “Make the complete loop launchable unattended: wake, evaluate, execute, record, and alert. Fix setup failures within the repair limit and verify a complete cycle plus recovery from an interrupted cycle.”
- **Next meaningful milestone:** “Complete the 24-hour soak under the agreed unattended-operation criteria and produce the qualification evidence. Record any implementation repair as a new candidate and restart the affected qualification window.”

A short experiment remains justified when it resolves a specific uncertainty blocking the milestone. State the uncertainty, bound the experiment, and identify the decision its result enables. Treat it as an internal implementation step, not the deliverable or a reason to stop.

## Qualification and evidence

Define acceptance before starting the qualification window:

- **Unattended operation:** For the initial service qualification, the deployed service must operate without human intervention or ad hoc implementation repairs by a coding agent. Recovery through already-deployed mechanisms may count if its behavior and limits were included in the acceptance criteria beforehand. Agent-assisted repair demonstrates a different capability and must be reported separately.
- **Useful work:** Specify the expected wake opportunities, required script/work coverage, correct outputs at the predetermined location, permitted missed or duplicate executions, heartbeat freshness, recovery limits, and evidence completeness. Elapsed time and a healthy heartbeat alone do not qualify the service.
- **Candidate identity:** Record the code/configuration version, environment, window start and end, and evidence locations. An implementation repair creates a new candidate; reset the affected qualification window when the repair invalidates its evidence. Do not splice incompatible candidates into one passing window.
- **Honest history:** Preserve failed attempts, repairs, resets, and unexpected failures alongside the final result. Distinguish expected fault-injection outcomes from unexpected failures. A passing recovery test does not erase a reliability failure.

## Repair authority and escalation

Autonomy covers implementation, not redefining success.

1. **Diagnose and repair within scope.** Proceed with routine, reversible repairs without requesting approval for each fix. One repair round consists of an evidence-backed diagnosis or hypothesis, a targeted repair attempt, and verification against the original acceptance criteria. A failed attempt counts; repeating the same command without new evidence is not progress. Use at most three rounds per unresolved blocker, within the milestone's stated time/resource budget.
2. **Stop at the boundary.** Escalate earlier for missing credentials or access, destructive changes, expanded spending or permissions, major architectural changes, unsafe state, or a decision outside existing authority. Three rounds is a ceiling, not a requirement to attempt unsafe or unsupported repairs. Do not reset the count by renaming a blocker, changing sessions, restarting the run, or creating a task.
3. **After three unsuccessful rounds, file a GitHub issue.** Stop attempting that blocker and file in the owning repository, or update an existing matching issue rather than creating a duplicate. Include the blocked capability, expected versus actual behavior, evidence locations, all three attempts and results, current safe state, qualification impact, and the decision or prerequisite needed to resume. Link the issue from the owning milestone and leave that milestone explicitly blocked or incomplete. If GitHub access is unavailable, retain the report locally and surface the filing blocker; do not claim it was filed.
4. **Move only to eligible work.** Once the failed work is safely stopped or isolated, select the next available task from the authorized work queue only if it is independent of the blocker, passes the same milestone gates, and is solvable with current machinery, credentials, permissions, and resources. Do not bypass a dependency or invent new tooling or busywork to stay active. Record the reason for the switch and the link to the blocked work.
5. **Otherwise remain honestly blocked or idle.** If no eligible task exists, report the blocker and the concrete condition needed to resume. Do not keep retrying the exhausted blocker on each scheduled wake. Resume it only after the recorded prerequisite changes or the operator explicitly authorizes a new repair budget; retain the prior attempt history.

This policy authorizes the blocker issue/report described above. It does not independently authorize repository pushes, merges, unrelated external publications, expanded spending, or expanded access. Existing explicit approvals and standing authorization remain in force.

Never weaken acceptance criteria, suppress errors, or count a repaired run as uninterrupted success. A blocked task remains visible when other work proceeds; moving on is not completion.

## Reusable collaborator instruction

```text
Before proposing a next milestone, answer:
1. What is the current agreed objective, what works now, and what observable
   capability will this milestone deliver?
2. Which current critical-path blocker does it remove?
3. What evidence will prove completion, what is the time/resource budget,
   and what would genuinely require operator intervention?

Proceed only when all three answers are concrete.

Own the milestone end to end. Diagnose and repair routine, reversible
failures without asking me to approve each fix. Use at most three repair
rounds per unresolved blocker: diagnosis, targeted repair, verification.
Keep the count and evidence across sessions and scheduled wakes.

After three unsuccessful rounds, stop that repair and file a GitHub issue
in the owning repository, or update an existing matching issue. Record
the attempts, evidence, safe state, qualification impact, and prerequisite
for resuming. Keep the owning milestone visibly blocked or incomplete.
If filing is unavailable, preserve the report and disclose the blocker.

Then move to the next available authorized task only if it is independent,
safe, passes the same gates, and is solvable with current machinery and
access. Otherwise report blocked or idle. Do not manufacture work, bypass
dependencies, or retry an exhausted blocker without a changed prerequisite
or an explicitly renewed repair budget.

Do not substitute plans, tiny experiments, or component checks for
delivery. Use them internally only when needed to complete the milestone.

Escalate immediately for missing credentials, destructive changes, expanded
spending or access, major architectural changes, or unsafe state.
Existing authorization boundaries remain in force.

Define unattended operation and useful-work acceptance before the run.
Distinguish deployed recovery from coding-agent repairs. Do not weaken
acceptance criteria, suppress errors, or count a repaired run as an
uninterrupted success. Record candidate versions, failures, repairs,
and qualification-window resets.

Report: capability delivered, verification evidence, remaining blocker,
repair rounds used, linked blocker issue, and the next eligible milestone
or the condition needed to resume.

Write milestone results as comments on the owning work issue. Include
evidence locations, repairs made, qualification-window resets, task switches,
and outstanding operator decisions. Use #1328 as the policy reference;
do not rewrite policy or acceptance criteria as part of routine reporting.
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The outer-loop collaborator's operating instructions include the three gates and repair-authority boundaries.
- [ ] Each proposed milestone names the current objective, observed baseline, concrete capability, critical-path justification, acceptance evidence, time/resource budget, and escalation conditions.
- [ ] Routine reversible blockers are handled within the milestone, with no more than three repair rounds per unresolved blocker and no counter reset across sessions or scheduled wakes.
- [ ] After three unsuccessful rounds, the collaborator files or updates a sourced GitHub issue, links it to the blocked milestone, and stops retrying until the stated resumption condition is met.
- [ ] The collaborator moves on only to an available, authorized, independent task that passes the gates and is safe and solvable with current machinery and access; otherwise it reports blocked or idle.
- [ ] Small experiments are bounded and tied to an explicit milestone-blocking uncertainty.
- [ ] Qualification criteria define unattended operation, useful work, permitted recovery, candidate identity, and evidence completeness before the window begins.
- [ ] Completion reports distinguish verified outcomes from attempts, unexpected failures, expected fault-injection results, and coding-agent repairs.
- [ ] Material repairs and qualification-window resets are recorded without weakening the acceptance criteria or discarding failed attempts.
- [ ] Milestone results are posted as comments on the owning work issue, referencing this policy.

## Non-goals

This issue does not select a new framework or model, change Jog's authority, authorize repository pushes or merges, or require a multi-adapter comparison. It establishes a reusable execution rubric for delivering agreed outer-loop milestones.
